chunks.arabic_text: وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ بَكَّارِ بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ فِي

translations.en: And it is narrated from Bakkār ibn Abī Bakr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning

chunks.arabic_text: الرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ لَهُ عَلَى الرَّجُلِ الْمَالُ فَإِذَا حَلَّ قَالَ لَهُ بِعْنِي مَتَاعًا حَتَّى أَبِيعَهُ وَ أَقْضِيَكَ الَّذِي لَكَ عَلَيَّ

translations.en: a man who has money owed to him by another man; when it becomes due, he says to him: "Sell me some goods so that I may sell them and repay you what is owed to you by me."
He عليه السلام said: "There is no harm in it."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a debt arrangement involving the sale of goods after a debt becomes due. Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام permits this transaction, indicating that such a sale for the purpose of enabling repayment is acceptable.
en.seo_question: Is it permissible for a debtor to buy goods on credit and sell them in order to repay a due debt?

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is permissible
